title: Noor and the Group Chat
premise: Wren Ishikawa, seventeen and functionally the parent of two younger siblings, has built their whole life around being unremarkable — until best friend Noor vanishes, leaving only a keyring and a cryptic group chat called 'the championship.' The chat pulls Wren into a hidden competition run by the enigmatic Alder Society, where belonging is the prize and the cost is everything you'd sacrifice for family. As Wren climbs the ranks, they discover Noor didn't disappear — she won, and winning means becoming one of them. In the end, Wren must choose between taking Noor's place in a family that promises never to need anyone, or walking away to the messy, exhausting family that actually needs them — and burning the Society's doors open so no one else gets 'chosen' again.
about_author: Astrid Montrose is the pen name of a former night-shift barista who wrote her first novel on break-room napkins while raising three younger brothers. She writes stories about kids who are older than they should have to be.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A day in the Ishikawa household: burnt dinners, forged permission slips, mom's night shift, and Wren's flawless performance of being fine at school. Establishes siblings Milo (12) and Junie (8) and Wren's friendship with radiant, restless Noor. Emotional beat: love expressed as logistics; loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Keys on the Windowsill
chapters.summary: Noor misses their standing Tuesday milkshake, then three days of school. Her mother assumes she ran off; police shrug. Wren finds Noor's house key, car key, and an unfamiliar brass key on her windowsill with a sticky note: 'win it for us.' POV Wren. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve — invisible people get ignored, so Wren stops being invisible.

chapters.title: You Have Been Added
chapters.summary: The brass key opens a locker at school containing a phone with one app: a group chat called 'the championship,' already populated by four other teens, each holding a key. A message from user ALDER: 'Round one begins Friday. Attendance is belonging.' POV Wren. Emotional beat: the intoxicating thrill of finally being chosen — and the first flicker of unease.

chapters.title: Round One
chapters.summary: Five competitors complete a midnight scavenger task across town that forces each to reveal a secret about their family. Wren wins by lying beautifully. Rival Theo notices the lie; quiet competitor Sam notices Wren's exhaustion. POV Wren, with chat-log interludes. Emotional beat: adrenaline and shame braided together — winning feels like being seen, which is also dangerous.

chapters.title: What Noor Left in Me
chapters.summary: Searching Noor's room, Wren finds her old journal: entries from last year's championship, growing darker as she 'rose.' She wrote that Alder promised a family that would never be disappointed in you. Wren hides it from the others. POV alternates Wren and Junie, who quietly knows something is wrong. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Ones Who Stay
chapters.summary: Milo gets suspended defending Wren's honor; mom's job threatens to cut hours. Home frays exactly when the championship demands more. Wren nearly quits — then ALDER offers a stipend that would cover rent. Theo catches Wren hesitating and confesses he's competing to escape his own family. POV Wren. Emotional beat: the seduction of being paid to abandon your real life.

chapters.title: Semifinals
chapters.summary: The semifinal task: competitors must convince someone they love to give up something irreplaceable. Wren refuses and cheats instead, trading secrets with Sam to survive. One competitor, Priya, completes it honestly — and vanishes like Noor. POV Wren. Emotional beat: horror crystallizing — the prize isn't belonging; it's replacement.

chapters.title: Alder House
chapters.summary: Following the brass key's second notch, Wren breaks into Alder House and finds the 'graduates': Noor, Priya, and dozens more, serene and hollow, folded into a found family that erased what they were. Noor doesn't remember the milkshakes. ALDER reveals the final round: become one of us, fully, or lose everything you've risked. POV Wren. Emotional beat: heartbreak — Noor is here, and gone.

chapters.title: The Championship That Matters
chapters.summary: Climax. Wren returns home, tells Milo and Junie everything, and asks for help — the thing they've never done. Together with Theo and Sam, they infiltrate the final ceremony, where Wren must 'win' by renouncing their family. Instead Wren names every graduate aloud, restoring their memories one by one, and lets the family they built storm the house. POV shifts among Wren, Noor waking, and Junie. Emotional beat: power refused; belonging reclaimed.

chapters.title: Fine, Actually
chapters.summary: Resolution. Alder House stands empty; the survivors keep a new group chat — just theirs, no tasks, no keys. Noor moves in with the Ishikawas while she relearns who she was. Mom takes a day shift; dinner is still burnt. Wren, finally, says out loud that things are not fine — and that's how they know they're okay. POV Wren. Emotional beat: found family as a choice renewed daily, not a prize.
